title: Impact of COVID-19 on Foreign Students Who Need to Serve Out Their Tuition Bonds
what_it_is: Impact of COVID-19 on Foreign Students Who Need to Serve Out Their Tuition Bonds

sections.label: International students on tuition grant
sections.summary: Over five years, tuition grant recipients averaged about 1,600 per cohort, under 10% of each intake, with similar trends expected for Academic Year 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Over the past five years, the number of international students who received tuition grant in each cohort averaged around 1,600, less than 10% of each intake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For Academic Year 2020, we are still finalising the numbers, but expect to see similar trends of less than 10%.

sections.label: Tuition grant holders' three-year bond
sections.summary: Supporting locals' employment remains the priority, but tuition grant holders with a three-year bond get fair treatment and can serve it in Singapore or overseas with Singapore-registered companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Our priority remains to support locals in finding employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: However, we will also give fair treatment to tuition grant holders obliged to serve a three-year bond after graduation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: These students can serve out their obligations in Singapore or overseas with Singapore-registered companies.

sections.label: Tuition grant holders and PR data
sections.summary: A Member asked about scholarship recipients' career paths and PR or Citizenship rates; the speaker lacked data on tuition grant holders applying for PR or Citizenship.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I am just curious if he could clarify the typical career path of scholarship recipients, in this case, especially in terms of the ratio of students who end up taking up Singapore Permanent Residence or Citizenship after they have completed their studies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: These Tuition Grant holders come in, they apply to the Universities; they do not need to apply for a Tuition Grant, but if they do so, they would have to serve a three-year bond.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I do not have on hand the data on the percentage of Tuition Grant holders who go on to apply for Permanent Residence (PR) or Citizenship, for that matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But just to make the point that Tuition Grant applicants and recipients are quite different from scholarship recipients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Again, if the Member would like to file a separate question asking for those details – number of scholarship holders, number of Tuition Grant holders – these are data that from time to time, Members in this House have asked for and we have released those data.
